key_insight: The paper shows that multiagent systems can produce a single, useful confidence score by calibrating individual agent signals and aggregating them with soft voting or Bayesian fusion, improving confidence discrimination without hurting answer accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable NLP pipelines where downstream systems can trust not just a final answer but also a system-level confidence for routing, oversight, and decision-making.
method: Transform raw confidence signals so outputs from different models become comparable.
Aggregate calibrated signals using soft voting or Bayesian fusion to produce one system-level confidence.
Compare sequence-probability and self-report estimators with parametric and non-parametric calibration across debate protocols.
evidence_signal: Across six homogeneous and heterogeneous debating pairs over five benchmarks and four task types, the proposed aggregated confidence improved AUARC over the best single agent and standard debate baselines while maintaining stable F1.
watch_item: The approach depends on calibration and careful comparability of confidence signals, so mismatched models or poorly calibrated estimators could weaken reliability.
paper_title: Multiagent Protocols with Aggregated Confidence Signals
